rule: **Objective-C++ (.mm)**: C++ constructs follow the C++ rules (`Cls::m` definitions, member calls, constructors); message sends follow the ObjC rules. | `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. | **C++**: namespace-qualified with dots: `ns.Class#method`, `ns.func`; `Class::static()` → `Class#static`; template arguments dropped.
source: KNOWN_GAP: inherited C++ members called bare (reportError) stay low
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. A bare call (and `this->` call) to `reportError`, which is defined only on the scanned superclass `eng::Base` → `eng.Base#reportError`, high. Out-of-line definitions `Base::reportError` / `Derived::run` inside namespace eng give `eng.Base#reportError` / `eng.Derived#run`. `d` is declared `eng::Derived *` → pointer names the pointee (Decision 2026-10-29). A low `reportError` guess would be wrong.
